ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED. The design is now established by construction rather than estimate, which is the useful output. Reverted cleanly to 364440c; the tree contains only closed-bead work.

WHAT WAS BUILT AND WORKED (all compiled green before revert):
- AgentMethod.ReadResults plus encodeRemoteResultReadsRequest / decodeRemoteResultReadsRequest / encodeRemoteResultReads / decodeRemoteResultReads, reusing the existing per-ref codecs so the batch shape is an array wrapper rather than new domain encoding.
- The agent handler, which is the reassuring part: it is deliberately the SAME per-ref read the single method performs, looped. The server does no new work. The entire saving is transport — one SSH process instead of one per pending element. It collapses AgentCalls so one failed read fails the group, because a partial answer would leave the caller unable to tell which refs were even attempted.
- SshAgentApi.readResults with a frame-budget guard: maximumBytes bounds EACH result, so a group is admitted only when maximumBytes * groupSize fits the negotiated typed-result budget, and an oversized group is a protocol failure rather than a truncated answer.

WHY IT WAS REVERTED — the blocker is not the protocol, it is the await loop.

RemoteBatchHandle.await is `elements.parTraverse(_.await)`, and each element's await is RemoteTaskHandle.poll, which owns semantics that took several beads to get right: exponential backoff, the 1-in-6 accounting probe cadence, riding out maximumConsecutiveObservationFailures transient failures, and distinguishing an await timeout from an observation failure ("I stopped being able to see the job" is the honest account).

Using readResults means a BATCH-LEVEL poller. That poller must either duplicate all of that logic — which creates two await implementations that will diverge, and this epic has already fixed several bugs caused by exactly that pattern (three hand-written terminality classifiers in A2, two DurableResultHandle constructions in D2) — or RemoteTaskHandle.poll must first be refactored so both paths share one implementation.

Shipping the protocol without that wiring leaves unused public surface, which I declined to do twice already in this epic (the LaunchSpec prototype in D1, and the compact Job surface in G1).

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE for whoever takes this:
1. P7.2 first. The batch DTOs are wire types; adding them before the ByteVector swap means hand-writing their codecs twice — the same constraint that ordered P6f.12 after P7.2.
2. Extract the tolerance/backoff/accounting/timeout logic out of RemoteTaskHandle.poll into something both a single-handle and a batch-level poller can share.
3. Then re-apply the protocol work above and wire the batch poller to it.

Step 2 is the real work and is worth doing on its own merits regardless of batching.
